English: Jungle Clearing
A simple patch of land cleared of dense jungle, serving as a rudimentary place of worship and gathering for the faithful.
Raised Shelter
A basic wooden platform raised above the forest floor, offering protection from the elements and a focal point for spiritual gatherings.
Wooden Jungle Shrine
A humble wooden shrine, adorned with sacred carvings and jungle flora, where priests lead prayers and rituals under the thick canopy.
Enclosed Jungle Hut
A sturdier hut built of thick timber and vines, offering improved shelter and privacy for religious study and meditation.
Thatched Sanctuary
A larger thatched sanctuary with open walls for airflow, housing sacred relics and attracting more followers for worship and learning.
Jungle Palisade
A fortified palisade of sharpened logs encircling the sanctuary, protecting the faithful and their treasures from wild beasts and raiders.
Jungle House
A large wooden house for priests and scholars, with separate chambers for learning, record-keeping, and religious instruction.
Jungle Gathering Hall
A broad hall with carved pillars and woven mats, where large assemblies, councils, and festivals reinforce faith and community.
Jungle Sanctuary
A richly decorated sanctuary with sacred idols, intricate wall paintings, and chambers for advanced theological study, drawing pilgrims from afar.
Jungle Temple
A grand temple of stone and timber, its sanctum veiled in incense and jungle blooms, housing relics and supporting a learned priesthood that influences the faith of the entire region.
